heroHeadline: Recession Probabilities Surge (May 16): Goldman 30% ↑, Moody's 49% ↑; BofA — No Fed Cuts Until July 2027; 10Y Yield 4.59% (Highest Since May 2025); Brent Crude $111; Section 122 Cliff July 23 (67 Days)
heroSubtitle: The week ending May 16, 2026 produced the sharpest post-summit reassessment of US recession risk in 2026. Goldman Sachs raised its US recession probability from ~20% to 30%; Moody's Analytics raised its estimate to 49% — approaching the 50% threshold where contraction becomes more probable than not. Bank of America withdrew all 2026 rate cut forecasts entirely, pushing the first Fed cut to July 2027 and pricing in >50% probability of at least one rate hike by March 2027. The catalyst: a week in which April CPI came in at 3.8% YoY (May 12), April PPI at +6.0% YoY (May 13 — hottest since December 2022), and the Trump-Xi Beijing summit concluded with 'meagre' outcomes — critically, no Iran/Hormuz breakthrough (Trump 'did not ask Xi for help'), leaving Brent crude at $111/bbl. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed the week at 4.59% — the highest since May 2025 — as bond markets priced out all 2026 cuts and began pricing potential hikes. Kevin Warsh officially assumed the 17th Federal Reserve Chair seat on May 15 (Powell term expired), inheriting the worst inflation backdrop since the Iran war began. S&P 500 closed at 7,408.50 (off ATH 7,501.24 set May 14); JPMorgan revised its 2026 S&P target down to 7,200. Partial offsets: April Retail Sales +4.9% YoY (consumer spending resilient) and Empire State Manufacturing 19.6 (highest since 2022). The Section 122 tariff cliff on July 23 (67 days away) remains the next critical policy trigger requiring Congressional action.
footerNote: Data sourced from TheStreet (Goldman Sachs 30% recession probability / BofA no-cut warning, May 2026), JPMorgan Mid-Year Outlook 2026 (35% recession probability), Moody's Analytics (49% recession probability), Federal Reserve H.15 / FRED DGS10 (10Y yield 4.59%, May 15), Fortune (Brent crude $111.04, May 15), IEA (Hormuz undersupply until October 2026), Sunday Guardian Live / Motley Fool (S&P 7,408.50 / Nasdaq 26,225.14 / Dow 49,526.17 May 15 close), CS Monitor / US News (Warsh assumes Fed Chair May 15), BLS April 2026 CPI (3.8% YoY, May 12), BLS April 2026 PPI (+6.0% YoY, May 13), US Census Bureau (April Retail Sales +4.9% YoY, May 15), Advisor Perspectives (Empire State Manufacturing 19.6, May 15).
